body.title: [sparkle] Align ButtonsSwitch with Button sizes, bordered track and pill
body.body:
## Description

`ButtonsSwitchList` was 6 to 12px taller than a `Button` of the same size because of its track padding, so the two did not line up in toolbars. The switch now takes the Button's height and radius per size (24 / 32 / 40px, 9 / 12 / 15px) with no inner padding; the options are plain Buttons again.

Visual tuning on top of that:
- The track gets the outline Button's border, drawn as an `after:` overlay over the options rather than a box border around them, so at the edges it coincides with the selected pill's border instead of doubling it.
- The sliding pill swaps its hairline and drop shadow for a 1px border (`border-dark`, stone-700 in dark) and a slight top-to-bottom gradient (white → stone-50, stone-725 → stone-750 in dark).

Ten `front` call sites use the switch (filters, theme selector, chart toggles); they all get shorter by 6 to 12px.

## Tests

`Sizes` story renders each size next to an outline Button and asserts the switch heights are exactly `[24, 32, 40]` and equal their neighbour's. 3 ButtonsSwitch browser tests pass; checked visually in light and dark.

## Risk

Layout shift in the `front` surfaces listed above where a switch sat in a row sized by the switch itself.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy sparkle.

body.title: [front] feat(i18n): format UI dates without date libraries
body.body:
## Description

Closes dust-tt/tasks#10692. Follows #33658.

Moves date formatting in UI code (`components/`, `hooks/`) off `date-fns`, `dayjs` and `luxon`:

- use `formatDateTime` with the new `NUMERIC_DATE_TIME_OPTIONS` where applicable
- use the new `formatTimeDistance` which wraps `intlFormatDistance` where applicable.
- use `formatDate` and `formatTime` where applicable
- pasted file names keep their fixed `yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss` pattern through `formatDate` of `lib/utils/timestamps`

Biome `noRestrictedImports` now rejects `dayjs`, `luxon` and the `format*`/`intlFormat*`/`lightFormat` imports of `date-fns` and `date-fns-tz` under `components/` and `hooks/`.

Not addressed here: date-fns helpers in `lib/` and `types/` (`dateToHumanReadable`, `getTime`, `formatCalendarDate*`, server and LLM-facing formatting).
The `dayjs` dependency is removed in #33704.

## Tests

`lib/i18n/format.test.ts`, run with `TZ=UTC`:
- In en-US, `formatDateTime(…, NUMERIC_DATE_TIME_OPTIONS)` equals date-fns `format(…, "Pp")`.
- `formatTimeDistance` equals `intlFormatDistance` from seconds to years, past and future, in both styles.
- `getPastedFileName` returns the same output in en-US and fr-FR

## Risk

Low.
- With the `localisation` flag off, the format locale is the browser's.
- The version labels were always rendered in the en-US pattern, so on non-English browsers they now follow the browser locale (`30/09/2026 16:11` in French).
- The relative distances already followed the browser locale through `intlFormatDistance`.

## Deploy Plan

Front only

## Description

Follow-up of dust-tt/tasks#10692.

Removes `dateToHumanReadable` from `types/shared/utils/date_utils.ts`. It formatted with date-fns `format(…, "MMM d, yyyy 'at' h:mm a")`. Its callers now call the module's `formatDateTime` with `dateStyle: "medium"` and `timeStyle: "short"`, as `SeatLimitScheduleDialog` and `SwitchContractDialog` already do:

body.title: [front] fix false positive tool name collision check
body.body:
## Description
This PR is to fix this ticket: https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/10456

MCP tool name must be [under 64 characters](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/986-specify-format-for-tool-names).  We normally add a server name prefix to a tool name like `gmail__get_message` and this needs to fit under the length limit. So when you have a very very long tool name, we don't prepend the server name, and in the ticket above one of the tool names was 62 characters. 

When you add a new MCP server, we run a check if the name doesn't conflict with the other server's tools you have. We don't fetch the actual tool names of each server but simply get the name of the server, prefix with the new tool name you are about to add, and check if it will be the same or not. So if you try to add Gmail, you check something like `gmail__get_message`  !== `[OTHER_SERVER_NAME]__get_message` etc etc. This check doesn't work when we drop the server prefix because whatever server name is the tool name will be always the same when we compare it. 

So we track if the server name prefix is dropped or not, and if it's dropped, we fetch all the tool names from other servers and compare if it's actually the same or not. This will be a slow query but given that this check only runs when a server is added or updated, and only when the prefix will be dropped, it should be safe.

body.title: [front] refactor(i18n): format calendar dates in the UI locale
body.body:
## Description

Follow-up of dust-tt/tasks#10692. Uses the same approach as #33774.

`formatCalendarDate` and `formatCalendarDateTime` move from `lib/utils/timestamps.ts` to `lib/client/calendar_date.ts` and format through the i18n module instead of date-fns `format`.

The date-fns day arithmetic (`isToday`, `differenceInCalendarDays`, …) stays as it is. Everything they render is formatted in the **UI locale**, like the relative times:
- "Today", "Yesterday" and "Tomorrow" come from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with `numeric: "auto"`, capitalized.
- Weekdays come from `formatDate(…, { weekday: "long" })`.
- Times come from `formatTime` with `timeStyle: "medium"` when they include seconds, `"short"` otherwise.
- The fallback date uses `formatDate` with `2-digit` day and month and a numeric year.

The connective words "Last" and "at" stay English, like "on" in `formatRelativeResetDay`.

### Visible English change (flag off, every user)

`formatCalendarDate`'s fallback, for dates more than a week away, was hardcoded `dd/MM/yyyy`. It's now the locale's numeric date, so en-US matches `formatCalendarDateTime`, which already used `MM/dd/yyyy`. It shows in the conversation date separator and on the dates of generated files.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `formatCalendarDate`, 8 days ago | `02/09/2026` | `09/02/2026` |

Every other en-US output is unchanged.

### With the flag on

| Locale | `formatCalendarDate` | `formatCalendarDateTime` |
|---|---|---|
| en-GB | `Yesterday`, `Last Sunday`, `02/09/2026` | `Today at 09:30:00`, `Tomorrow at 00:00` |
| fr-FR | `Hier`, `Last dimanche`, `02/09/2026` | `Aujourd’hui at 09:30:00`, `Demain at 00:00` |

"Last" and "at" stay English until these helpers are translated.

Also drops the date-fns `format` import from `types/shared/utils/date_utils.ts`. It became unused on main once #33781 and #33782 both merged, each having removed one of its two users, and it fails `biome ci`.

## Tests

`lib/client/calendar_date.test.ts` takes over the existing cases from `timestamps.test.ts`, with the fallback date updated. It adds en-GB and fr-FR, and checks that the format locale has no effect.

## Risk

Low: one English date order change, described above.

## Deploy Plan

Front only

body.title: security: deny file reads that are not explicitly authorized

labels.name: documentation-ack
labels.description: Used to acknowledge that documentation is up-to-date with this PR

body.body:
## What was wrong

Anywhere the app looked up a file by its `fil_` id, it treated "this file exists in your workspace" as "you are allowed to read it." File ids are sequential under the hood, so any workspace member can guess other members' file ids. That opened three doors:

1. **Download other members' files.** `GET /api/w/:wId/files/:fileId` only checked permissions for two file types: folder documents, and conversation files that already had a conversation attached. Everything else (CSV tables uploaded to a restricted space, pending uploads, avatars, branding images, skill attachments) was handed to any member. The metadata route and the public `/api/v1` file route had the same gap, and so did replace (`POST`) and `DELETE`.
2. **Learn which conversation a file belongs to.** When the MCP `files_resolve` tool (and the agent-loop resolver) was asked for a file with the wrong scope, it replied with `Resolved path: conversation-<id>/report.pdf` before checking the caller could see that conversation. Knowing a conversation id is often enough to open it, so this was a way into other members' conversations.
3. **Copy another member's CSV into your own table.** The table upsert endpoints accept a `fileId` and ingest that CSV. They never checked whether the caller could read the file, so pointing them at a victim's CSV exposed its contents through the attacker's own table.

## The fix

One function, `canReadSourceFile(auth, file)`, that starts from "no" and only says "yes" when the file's use case grants it:

| Use case | Granted when |
| --- | --- |
| `conversation`, `tool_output` | caller can open the conversation, or the file is not attached yet and the caller uploaded it |
| `folders_document`, `project_context` | caller can read the file's space |
| `upsert_table` | caller can read the file's space, or no space is set and the caller uploaded it |
| `skill_attachment` | caller can read a skill that references the file, or the pending skill it was uploaded for, or (no skill yet) the caller uploaded it |
| `workspace_branding` | caller uploaded it or is an admin |
| `upsert_document`, `avatar` | caller uploaded it |
| any use case | caller is a system key (connectors, internal services), which already holds wildcard grants |

Every file-by-id read now calls it first: the session download / metadata / replace / delete routes, the public v1 route, both resolve tools, and both CSV ingest paths (before any bytes are read). A denied caller gets the same 404 a nonexistent file gets. Resolve errors no longer contain the path, file name, conversation id, or pod id.

## What changes for users

Nothing for legitimate use. You can still read your own uploads, files in spaces you belong to, and files in conversations you can open. Response schemas are unchanged. The only requests that now fail are reads of files the caller was never granted, which now return 404.

## Test plan
Full test coverage added

## Deploy Plan
1. Deploy front

## Review
r? @id13 (since this is file system adjacent)

body.title: redirect eu front edge
body.body:
## Description
When you open a preview app for front-edge EU, we first make `/auth-context` to the US edge server. This correctly returns to redirect to EU but the URL is the production URL and not edge. 

The SPA is built with `/.env.edge` config:
https://github.com/dust-tt/dust/blob/dde6640a16070e62708cbdb83b7160bc93f2cf88/.github/configs/us-central1/.env.edge#L1-L4

The workflow turns `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values into `VITE_*` values (this part I don't know why it's called NEXT). 
When the page loads, `CellProvider` chooses a cell to call in these order (I also don't know why we have so many):
 ```
1. the ?cell= URL param
2. the ?region= URL param (older links)
3. the cell saved in localStorage
4. the region saved in localStorage (older browsers)
5. otherwise the build's default cell, VITE_DUST_CELL
```
In our case it goes to VITE_DUST_CELL, which will be resolved to `VITE_DUST_API_URL_US`, which is correct US front edge address for edge SPA build. 

Now on the server side, it returns with a 400 if a request comes from EU workspace with the redirect URL from `DUST_EU_URL`. 

Preview URLs can come from front edge or GitHub preview app when you add a label. We don't want to use front edge when it's generated by a GitHub label so we don't want to decide if we should return edge redirect url or not based on where the request coming from. 

Given that the client already know all the URLs we need, we don't take redirect URL from the server's response, take only its name, and resolve the URL on the client side.

body.title: [front] Guard parser against infinite loop on string-embedded closing parens
body.body:
## Description

`checkBalancedParentheses` counts raw `(` / `)` characters without understanding string literals. An input like `(")")` passes the balance check (one real `(`, one `)` inside the string, one trailing `)` = balance 0) but leaves no actual closing paren for `parseList`. After consuming the `)` inside the string literal, `parseList` reaches the end of the expression, but the while-condition `expression[index] !== ")"` evaluates to `undefined !== ")"` → `true`, causing an infinite loop as `parseAtom` repeatedly returns `Ok("")` without advancing.

Added an explicit `index >= expression.length` guard at the top of the loop body that returns an error instead.

## Tests

Biome and actionlint pass on CI. Legitimate well-formed expressions are unaffected; only malformed inputs that hit end-of-string before a closing paren now error out instead of looping.

## Risk

Low — the fix only adds an early-exit on an impossible-to-reach state for valid inputs. Malformed inputs previously caused CPU spin; now they return a parse error.

## Deploy plan

deploy front

## Review
r? @pmilliotte

body.title: feat(discovery): rank For you by best size-weighted group adoption
body.body:
## Description

**Before:** each item's adoption summed over the viewer's groups, adjusted by confidence and small-group boosts, with items the viewer already used hidden.

**Now:** each item's score in its best group, `users / activeUsers^1.7`, so small groups weigh more and overlapping big groups don't stack. Dust-provided skills are excluded and items the viewer uses stay in.

## Tests

Unit tests updated, checked on a test env.

## Risk

Low. Same group pool queries, one less query per viewer. The pool cache key moves to v2, so pools are rebuilt once.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy front

body.title: security(front-api): force attachment for unsafe inline file-serving (SVG/HTML XSS)
body.body:
## Summary

Five front-api routes streamed stored GCS files inline using the raw stored
content type without checking `isSafeToDisplay`. An attacker who can upload a
file with `image/svg+xml` (or another unsafe type like `text/html`) as its
stored content type could cause the browser to render it on the app origin,
enabling stored XSS.

Root cause: `isSupportedImageContentType` (used in thumbnail routes) includes
`image/svg+xml` because its format category is `"image"` — but
`isSafeToDisplay` for SVG is `false`. The general file-serving routes had no
content-type check at all.

**Fix pattern (general serving routes):** add `isContentTypeSafeToDisplay` check
(mirrors `getFileFormat(normalizeMimeType(ct))?.isSafeToDisplay`) and force
`Content-Disposition: attachment` for unsafe types.

**Fix pattern (thumbnail routes):** reject with HTTP 400 — thumbnails are
inline-only previews, so forcing a download is not a useful fallback.


## Findings fixed

| Row | Finding | File | Lines |
|-----|---------|------|-------|
| L44 | Inline SVG/HTML serving via GCS content type | `front-api/routes/w/[wId]/assistant/conversations/[cId]/files/thumbnail.ts` | 87–95, 123–131 |
| L56 | Inline SVG/HTML serving via GCS content type | `front-api/routes/w/[wId]/spaces/[spaceId]/files/[...rel].ts` | 130–141 |
| L58 | Inline SVG/HTML serving via GCS content type | `front-api/routes/w/[wId]/assistant/conversations/[cId]/files/[...rel].ts` | 96–107 |
| L90 | Inline SVG/HTML serving via GCS content type | `front-api/routes/w/[wId]/skills/[sId]/files/[fileId]/content.ts` | 54–57 |
| L93 | Inline SVG/HTML serving — thumbnail path without safety check | `front-api/routes/w/[wId]/files/path/[...canonicalPath].ts` | 404–412 |

## Risk

Low

## Deploy Plan
1. Deploy front

body.title: fix: scan Tailwind arbitrary values in linear time
body.body:
## Description

Superseeds #33518.

`validateTailwindCode` used `/\b[a-z-]+-\[[^\]]+\]/g` to find arbitrary values in `className` attributes. The regex is quadratic in the className length: `[a-z-]+` backtracks at every split of a long hyphenated run, and `[^\]]+\]` rescans to the end of the string for every unclosed `[`. Frame edits run this synchronously, so any workspace member can POST a crafted className and stall the front event loop.

#33518 rewrote the regex as `/\b[a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*-\[[^\]]+\]/g`. That removes the hyphen ambiguity but the engine still restarts at every word boundary and rescans the suffix, so it stays quadratic (cc-verify flagged it on the PR). It also drops matches like `a--[y]` that the old regex flagged.

This PR replaces the regex with a single-pass scanner: match `\b[a-z-]+`, require a trailing `-` followed by `[`, `indexOf("]")` once, resume after the match. If no `]` exists after the current `[`, no later candidate can close either, so the scan stops. Output is identical to the old regex.

| input | old regex | #33518 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"a-".repeat(10_000) + "a"` | 232 ms | 254 ms | <1 ms |
| `"a-".repeat(20_000) + "a"` | ~1 s | 1015 ms | <1 ms |
| `"h-[".repeat(20_000)` | ~500 ms | 470 ms | <1 ms |

## Tests

New tests in `content_validation.test.ts`: both pathological inputs at 40k repeats must complete under 1 s, and a parity test locks the old regex's behavior on variants, negative utilities, empty `[]` and nested `[`.

## Risk

Worst case a false positive or negative on an exotic arbitrary value, which only changes a non-blocking warning sent back to the agent. Safe to rollback.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy front.

body.title: Open the knowledge browser alone from composers without capabilities
body.body:
The Agent Builder's preview and sidekick composers offer attachments but no capabilities, so the flag removal left them on the old plus menu and attachments picker while the main composer moved to the slash menu. This gives them the slash menu too, locked to attaching: the "+" inserts "/" as in the main composer, and the menu that opens is the knowledge browser alone. The text after "/" is the browser's query, there is no Back row to a command list, no skill or tool is fetched, and Escape or Backspace at the browser's root closes the menu. Inside the browser nothing changes: spaces, folders, scoped and global search, Add on a data source. The one addition is a Files section at the bottom of the browser's root carrying the composer's Upload file command, since the plus menu these composers had offered file upload and the browser alone has no other place for it; it sits last so the first space stays the default highlight and Enter still enters it.

A composer's mode comes from its actions through `getInputBarSlashMenuMode`: `commands` with the capabilities action, `attach-only` with attachments alone, none otherwise. The container passes it to the extension by ref like the other menu options; the extension allows a leading space after "/" in attach-only mode, since the text is a search query. The dropdown renders the attach sub-menu directly in that mode, with the sub-menu's frame and Back made optional and a root section it can host, and asks the capabilities hook to stay idle through a new `disabled` flag so nothing is fetched for a menu that cannot show it. The shared dropdown treated the Back row as the thing that kept a sub-menu's sections and breadcrumbs on screen; it now counts a section's own loading rows or empty message, and a header, as content, so a search with no matches below the root keeps its crumbs and its loading placeholders without a Back row. The Chrome extension composer is excluded and keeps its own "+" menu.

Stacked on `33396`, which fixes the browsing edge cases these composers would otherwise hit first. The plus menu and attachments picker now serve only the extension composer; deleting them is the next PR.

## Tests

- Unit tests on the mode derivation and on the sections' own-state check; the slash-menu, browser and input bar suites pass; `tsgo`, `biome` and `cc-check` clean.
- To check on the preview, in the Agent Builder: the Preview and Sidekick "+" open the knowledge browser with "Type to search" after the slash; typing filters it; there is no Back row; Escape closes; Backspace from a folder walks up and closes at the spaces list; Upload file sits in a Files section below Spaces and Pods at the root and opens the file dialog, while Enter on an empty query still enters the first space; the main composer's "/" menu is unchanged.

## Risk

Low. The commands mode is untouched apart from the new mode check; attach-only is only reached by composers that had no slash menu before. Rollback is a revert.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy `front`.

body.title: [connectors] fix: relaunch Google Drive incremental sync with policy

labels.name: PMRR
labels.description: Add when you PMRR so that z can find them easily

body.body:
## Description

We are seeing a few issues we missing Google drive workflows a day ([example](https://app.datadoghq.eu/logs?query=%22Production+check+failed%22+cell%3Acell-00000+-%40errorMessage%3A%22Google+Drive+documents+not+properly+Garbage+collected%22&from_ts=1790825277000&to_ts=1790829177000&live=false&agg_m=count&agg_t=count&index=%2A&event=AwAAAaD1vCRZZ54yRAAAABhBYUQxdkNkakFBQnBkMzNqLWtCSTJnQUcAAAAkZjFhMGY1YmQtMGYzNy00MjgxLWE0YmMtZmIxODFkMDIzNWNkAAAlLA)).
There's a pattern across all occurrences where the latest incremental syncs failed due with `"Workflow execution already started"` ([example](https://cloud.temporal.io/namespaces/dust-prod.gmnlm/workflows/googleDrive-IncrementalSync-16929/01a0f2f5-17e4-7995-88a2-83c9200537ce/history)) while the one before was terminated ([example](https://cloud.temporal.io/namespaces/dust-prod.gmnlm/workflows/googleDrive-IncrementalSync-16929/9a6050d6-82ca-47d9-8af7-d42d5574d23a/history)).

My assumption is that there's a race condition in the `setPermissions` path where the termination does not come in time before the launch of the new workflow (maybe rate limits, SDK buffering). This PR replaces the manual terminate + launch new with a `TERMINATE_EXISTING` conflict policy on the new workflow start to replace the running workflow in one request.

`workflowIdConflictPolicy` is available on our version of temporal server (we upgraded at some point), already used in the metronome queue and the sandbox reaper.

## Tests

## Risk

- Low.

## Deploy Plan

- Deploy connectors.

body.title: Remove the input bar plus menu
body.body:
With the "+" opening the slash menu in every composer that has attachments or capabilities, the plus menu component is reachable only from a composer with neither, where it rendered nothing. This deletes it, along with the eight props of the input bar buttons that existed only to feed it: the node select handler, the five space-selection props and the two open-change callbacks, and the container's handlers behind them.

No behaviour changes. The main composer, the Agent Builder preview and sidekick keep the slash menu; the analytics panel keeps having no "+"; the Chrome extension composer keeps the "+" the container builds for it, which renders the attachments picker directly and never went through the plus menu. That picker, and the capabilities picker the plus menu wrapped, stay for their remaining callers.

The composer action list and its type move out of the container into `inputBarActions.ts`, so the slash menu types module stops type-importing from the container that imports it. React Doctor flagged the buttons component's complexity on the first push, so its agent pill, agent button, capabilities button (which now owns the setup dialog state) and hidden file input become focused components in the same file, with the main component left as layout; rendering order and behaviour are unchanged.

Stacked on `33577`. Whether the extension composer should move to the slash menu too, and take the attachments picker with it, is a separate decision.

## Tests

- Input bar, editor and Agent Builder suites pass; `tsgo` and `biome` clean; React Doctor no longer flags the buttons component (its two remaining warnings are pre-existing on the container and the shared dropdown).
- To check on the preview: the main composer, Preview and Sidekick "+" all open the slash menu; the extension build's "+" still shows Attach and its picker.

## Risk

None expected. Deletion of an unreachable component and the plumbing that fed it.
